name: LiquidCompute API
description:
LiquidCompute provides read-only GPU price index and current vendor-price
data over HTTPS. All comparable values use USD per GPU-hour. Dates and timestamps
are UTC.

## Quickstart

Set your API key:

```sh
export LIQUIDCOMPUTE_API_KEY="your_liquidcompute_api_key"
```

Check service health. This endpoint is public and does not require an API key:

```sh
curl "https://api.liquidcompute.co/health"
```

Fetch the latest H100 custom index value:

```sh
curl -H "X-API-Key: $LIQUIDCOMPUTE_API_KEY" \
  "https://api.liquidcompute.co/v1/custom-index/current?region_group=US&contract_type=combined&vendor_category=neocloud"
```

Fetch daily transaction index data:

```sh
curl -H "X-API-Key: $LIQUIDCOMPUTE_API_KEY" \
  "https://api.liquidcompute.co/v1/txn-index/current?gpu_family=hopper&region_group=US&contract_type=combined"
```

Fetch informational history:

```sh
curl -H "X-API-Key: $LIQUIDCOMPUTE_API_KEY" \
  "https://api.liquidcompute.co/v1/info-index/history?index_name=hopper&region_group=US&start_date=2026-01-01"
```

Fetch the current vendor-price snapshot:

```sh
curl -H "X-API-Key: $LIQUIDCOMPUTE_API_KEY" \
  "https://api.liquidcompute.co/v1/gpu-prices/current"
```

## Authentication

Send your LiquidCompute API key in the `X-API-Key` header on every `/v1`
request. Missing or invalid keys return `401`. A validation-service
failure returns `503`; it is never reported as invalid credentials.
Create a new LiquidCompute API key during production onboarding.

```http
X-API-Key: your_liquidcompute_api_key
```

## Entitlements

Access to every data family — custom, transaction, and informational
indices, private transactions, GPU prices, and reference series — is
governed by your organization's entitlements. Requests for an index, or
an index family, outside your entitlements return `404` `not_found`.
Intraday custom index history (30-minute and hourly resolutions)
additionally requires the `intraday` family.

## Rate Limits

Limits are token buckets per API key: you can burst up to your bucket
size and sustain your refill rate. Metadata is returned in response
headers after parameter validation and authorization checks (during rare
degraded operation the `X-RateLimit-*` headers may be omitted;
`Retry-After` is still set on the gateway's own `429` responses):

| Header | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Your bucket size (burst capacity) |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Tokens currently available |
| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | Unix timestamp of the estimated next-token time |
| `Retry-After` | Seconds to wait; always present for `rate_limited` and `data_unavailable` (gateway default of 300 s when the upstream sends no hint), and forwarded for `upstream_rate_limited` when supplied |

Two distinct `429` codes: `rate_limited` means your key's bucket is
empty; `upstream_rate_limited` means the shared upstream data source is
throttled. `Retry-After` is always present for both codes; when the
upstream omits a hint, the gateway returns `Retry-After: 1`.

## Response Headers

Every response includes `X-Request-Id`. Quote it when reporting a failed
request; the same value is logged by the gateway and forwarded upstream.

`/v1/custom-index/available` and `/v1/custom-index/reference` vary by API
key. Their successful responses therefore include
`Cache-Control: private, no-store` and `Vary: X-API-Key`; upstream cache
headers are never forwarded on those two routes.

## Errors

Errors are returned as JSON.

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "not_found",
    "message": "Endpoint not found"
  }
}
```

Common statuses:

| Status | Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | `invalid_request` | Invalid or unsupported query parameter |
| `401` | `unauthorized` | Missing or invalid API key |
| `404` | `not_found` | Unknown endpoint, unavailable resource, or an index or index family outside your authorization |
| `405` | `method_not_allowed` | Method not allowed; only GET is supported |
| `429` | `rate_limited` | Your key's rate limit was exceeded |
| `429` | `upstream_rate_limited` | The shared upstream data source is throttled; retry shortly |
| `502` | `upstream_error` | The upstream data source is unavailable |
| `502` | `configuration_error` | Gateway-side configuration failure |
| `503` | `service_unavailable` | API-key validation is temporarily unavailable |
| `503` | `data_unavailable` | The data behind this endpoint has not been produced yet; retry after `Retry-After` |
